html:
SMTO-WEB-0053 — SMTO couldn't save a downloaded PDF for this task

GUID: 34d04ce2-9320-5dfb-9e96-fc3b2f68d5f8
Slug: web-document-materialization-failed
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't store the PDF in this task's files, so it can't read or quote it. This can happen when the server's disk is full, the task's file space is used up, or the task was closed or deleted.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure this task is still open and wasn't deleted, then send a new message asking SMTO to read the document again. SMTO can only save files into a task that still exists.
  2. If this task has already created many files, start a new conversation and ask about the document there. Each task has a limit on how many files and how much space it may use, and a new conversation starts with an empty allowance.
  3. Ask the person who manages SMTO to check that the computer running the SMTO server has free disk space. A full disk stops SMTO from saving any downloaded file.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's activity shows the PDF was saved, and its answer quotes pages from it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rely on quotes from this PDF until SMTO reports it saved the file.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PDF acquisition could not register the document in the run's artifact store: no artifact store or run/conversation scope was available, or ArtifactStore registration failed (retired or deleted workspace, per-run quota, disk or I/O error).

What this means

  • PDF acquisition lacks an artifact store or run/conversation scope, artifact registration fails, or materialization cannot provide the run's usable document path. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • PDF acquisition lacks an artifact store or run/conversation scope, artifact registration fails, or materialization cannot provide the run's usable document path.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect artifact registration versus Gateway materialization status and any retained complete artifact reference.

How to fix it

  • web/documents.acquire() raises document_materialization_failed when the context lacks _artifact_store or run_id/conversation_id scope, or store.register_chunks() raises a non-cancel error. Inspect the server log for the underlying ArtifactError, check AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_RUN_BYTES and AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_RUN_COUNT and free space under the artifact store; a later Gateway handoff failure does not raise this code. Do not claim the PDF exists until registration completes.
  • Check the run artifact workspace and selected Gateway transfer availability. Retained complete artifacts can be reused; do not cite unextracted bytes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • A complete artifact is materialized through the supported route before extraction supplies cited evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not claim a PDF artifact exists when materialization did not complete.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
